recent.summary: ORCL surged +10.7% on blowout earnings and explicit 2030 cash flow guidance, directly countering AI spending fears and sparking a broad risk-on rally in semis and cloud infrastructure (MU +5.86%, AVGO reaffirmed BUY). MSFT's Azure beat after hours provided a second confirming catalyst for AI infra demand, while GOOGL's negative free cash flow and capex blowout dragged Mega-cap Tech sentiment, leaving META as the session's standout laggard (-1.24% on a green tape). Capital rotation is firmly into AI infrastructure and semis, with META and PLTR facing valuation compression and the Fed holding rates at 3.75–4.0% with a hawkish lean adding pressure on rate-sensitive growth names.

Markets split sharply as GOOGL posted its worst single-day drop ever (-12.6%) on structural search revenue fears and AMZN missed profits on soaring AI capex, dragging Big Tech and semis lower. Defense stocks surged for an 8th+ consecutive day led by LHX (+6.84%) on a blowout Q3 with $11B in missile defense awards and FCF +195%, confirming robust DoD spending. Capital rotation out of growth and into defense, healthcare, and consumer staples is accelerating, with active BUY signals on LHX, RTX, and LLY and a high-conviction SELL on GOOGL.

The Nasdaq is on pace for its worst month in over a year as an AI spending reckoning deepens — INTC cratered 28.6% post-earnings, dragging QCOM (-11.1%), NVDA (-5.3%), and DDOG (-11.5%) down in a sector-wide semiconductor breakdown, while Amazon's revenue and EPS miss on soaring AI capex compounded the selloff. Capital is rotating hard out of AI/growth into Energy (XOM +2.2%, CVX +1.8%) and Consumer Staples (WMT +1.9%), supported by Strait of Hormuz tanker fires and a US evacuation order from Saudi Arabia driving a geopolitical oil premium. Multiple open BUY signals across semis and AI names (NVDA, DDOG, AVGO, AMD) are deeply underwater, confirming the rotation thesis was not acted on fast enough and demanding tighter sell discipline.

The Nasdaq dropped 1%+ to open November as AI/cloud names cratered — ORCL and INTC each fell ~8.8% on capex overhang and PC weakness — while consumer staples (WMT +3.4%, COST +2.8%) surged on a broad growth-to-defensive rotation. AMZN was a standout exception, rallying 2.2% on a strong post-earnings beat across both AWS and e-commerce, while GOOGL and DDOG continued multi-session downtrends with no fundamental reversal in sight. Energy sold off sharply as US-Iran deal hopes eroded the geopolitical premium, putting the open XOM BUY under pressure and reinforcing the need for tighter stops on geopolitical longs.

A broad risk-on Election Day rebound is led by crypto-adjacent Bitcoin miners (MARA +11%, Riot +14%), AI semis (AMD blowout earnings), and cloud (ORCL +5.8% squeezing an open SELL), while consumer staples (WMT, COST) and energy sell off as Iran geopolitical premium fades. Key BUY signals are initiated on AMD (fresh earnings catalyst), COIN (Tether BTC reserve disclosure), and AMZN (reaffirmed on AWS dual beat), while AAPL and PLTR are flagged as SELLs on persistent relative weakness and Cramer warnings. Track record remains challenged at 47%/33% win rate with ORCL SELL now at max loss and NVDA SELL working against an active semi rebound.

A Democratic congressional sweep triggered the biggest post-midterm Dow rally in 44 years (+3%), with mega-cap tech (MSFT +6.7%, AMZN +6.1%) and consumer names (MCD +6.5%) surging on election clarity and rotation into lower-risk sectors. Defense (LMT -6.9%) and energy (XOM -4.6%) cratered as Vance repudiated the Iran war and Democratic policy shifts erased geopolitical risk premiums. DDOG collapsed 14.4% on a beat-and-lower earnings reaction, reinforcing that AI/cloud remains treacherous even on strong fundamentals, while the open AMZN BUY from $245.63 extended to +8.3%.

The Nasdaq plunged 5.5% into correction territory — its worst chip selloff since Covid — fully erasing the post-election rally as AI spending fears and Democrat data center regulation concerns crushed semis (MU -17.5%, AMD -17.3%, TSM -10.8%) and crypto-adjacent names (MARA -14.5%). Capital rotated hard into defensive safe-havens, with COST and SAP the only green names in a 30-stock universe. Key signals: AMD BUY cut at -16.4% loss, NVDA re-entered at oversold levels (MEDIUM confidence), PLTR SELL extended to +11.6% gain, and AMZN BUY held resilient at +6.0%.

weekly.summary: A BofA AI bubble warning, CoreWeave credit stress, and VIX spiking above 22 triggered a four-session, $260B+ risk-off unwind crushing high-multiple AI, cloud, and crypto names (PLTR, SNOW -8%+, MSTR -9.6% with added MSCI removal headwinds, MARA -9.6%). Capital rotated decisively into Defense (RTX +3.7%, LMT +3.6%) and Energy (CVX +2.6%) on Middle East escalation via Yemen missile strikes and a US SPR solicitation, while AAPL held as the lone resilient core-tech name on iPhone demand, Chinese subsidies, and Berkshire support. Core calls — **BUY RTX, LMT, AAPL; SELL PLTR, MSTR** — remained fully intact across all sessions.

**Week Summary (3 sentences):**

AI/cloud and cybersecurity (DDOG, NET, AMZN) were the dominant BUY themes, fueled by SpaceX compute demand, PHP vulnerability spikes, and Iran escalation-driven infrastructure bids — with NET and DDOG delivering strong gains — though the Nasdaq's worst session since June, triggered by chipmaking supply warnings and META AI spending fears, crushed semis (AMD -8.1%, INTC -8.0%) and pulled the broader growth complex below its 50-day MA. Defense was a major early-week driver via NOC's $110B backlog, LMT's ~7% F-35 surge, and RTX read-across BUYs, but geopolitical risk-premium fading and Ukraine peace talk resumption sparked a late-week rotation out of the sector, while capital shifted defensively into cybersecurity and energy infrastructure as Iran escalation entered day two. MSTR and PLTR SELLs were badly burned (-12.2% and -8.4%) by crypto regulatory clarity and the AI rebound, AAPL was downgraded on foldable sell-the-news risk, and AMZN BUY was closed at -5.5% and flipped to SELL ahead of earnings — leaving NET (+6.0%), DDOG (+3.6%), and LMT (+2.4%) as the week's cleanest working calls.

**Week Summary:** AI optimism, sparked by Anthropic's IPO filing confirming surging chip demand, drove broad gains across semiconductors (AMD +5.45%, AVGO +4%, NVDA BUY initiated) and cloud names, while defense extended its rally (LMT +5.1%, RTX +3.4%) before retreating late on Iran diplomacy signals easing geopolitical risk premiums. Boeing was the week's standout loser (-10.69%) on a confirmed Q3 earnings disaster of missed deliveries and slashed production, and crypto-adjacent names MSTR and META underperformed the otherwise risk-on tape. The dominant binary risks ahead are MSFT, GOOGL, and AMZN earnings plus the Fed decision, with META flagged as a live SELL and AMZN on WATCH for post-print confirmation.
